numerical_failure.observed_behavior: With missing values (NaN) present in X, the tree is sometimes built incorrectly: the last non-missing sample is not partitioned correctly, so the computed impurity is not [0.25 0. 0.] but [0.25 0.1875 0.1875] and the tree has fewer leaves than expected (about half of fits give 1 leaf instead of 2; np.bincount of n_leaves over 1000 fits prints roughly [0 ~500 ~500] instead of all 2-leaf trees).
numerical_failure.expected_behavior: The tree should always have two leaves and impurity [0.25 0. 0.] for the reproducer, i.e. the impurity decrease should be computed correctly and all trees should have two leaves (assert tree.tree_.n_leaves == 2 holds on every fit).
trigger_conditions: X contains missing values (NaN) in a feature, created by X[X == 0] = np.nan
min_impurity_decrease set (0.25 in the issue reproducer, 0.002 in the PR snippet) together with max_depth=1
the problem occurs only if a different feature is examined first before the feature with missing values
fails roughly half the time across random states (about 50% of fits)

input_output_examples.input: X = np.vstack([[0,0,0,0,1,2,3,4],[1,2,1,2,1,2,1,2]]).swapaxes(0,1).astype(float); y=[0,0,0,0,1,1,1,1]; X[X==0]=np.nan; DecisionTreeRegressor(max_depth=1, min_impurity_decrease=0.25).fit(X, y) repeated 1000 times
input_output_examples.buggy_output: np.bincount(n_leaves_w_missing) prints approximately [0 ~500 ~500], i.e. about half the trees have 1 leaf
input_output_examples.expected_output: all trees have two leaves; tree.tree_.n_leaves == 2 for every fit

input_output_examples.input: same X and y with NaN as above, DecisionTreeRegressor(max_depth=1, random_state=i, min_impurity_decrease=0.002).fit(X, y) for broken random state i=2

oracle_clues: non-regression test: repeatedly fit and check the computed impurity / n_leaves over about 20 to 50 fits; the bug should trigger in ~50% of fits
assertion assert tree.tree_.n_leaves == 2 in the issue reproducer
impurity values compared: expected [0.25 0. 0.] versus buggy [0.25 0.1875 0.1875]
fix: examine one more value so all non-missing values are considered in partitioning (off-by-one in partitioning with missing values)

category_specific_evidence: Reproducer X is cast with astype(float) and y is [0,0,0,0,1,1,1,1]; with max_depth=1 and min_impurity_decrease=0.25 the tree should always have two leaves when there are no missing values.
After X[X == 0] = np.nan, the issue reports that about half of 1000 fits yield one leaf (bincount approx [0 ~500 ~500]), instead of always two leaves.
The violated property is that the impurity decrease computed with missing values is wrong, so trees are unexpectedly shallow when min_impurity_decrease controls depth.
Regression test expects tree.tree_.impurity to equal [0.25, 0.0, 0.0] for each of 20 random_state values; the broken case shows [0.25, 0.1875, 0.1875] instead.
PR debugging output for a broken random state shows best_n_missing=4 with partition_end=3 on start=0 end=7, indicating the last non-missing sample was not partitioned correctly (off-by-one).
Commit message: the fix examines one more value so all non-missing values are considered; the bug reportedly occurs in about 50% of fits.
reproduction_risks: Bug is random-state dependent (depends on which feature is tried first), so a single fit may not reproduce it; repeated fits (about 20 to 1000) are needed.
The exact fraction of broken trees is approximate (~50%) and may vary across runs.
Reproducer relies on NaN replacement of zeros in X, which changes the feature ordering behavior; results depend on the sklearn version before the fix.

provenance.value: OpenBLAS via numpy/scipy bundled libscipy_openblas (threadpoolctl reports openblas 0.3.30 and 0.3.29.dev, architecture Haswell); OpenMP via libgomp; not explicitly documented as a requirement

With missing values (NaN) present in X, the tree is sometimes built incorrectly: the last non-missing sample is not partitioned correctly, so the computed impurity is not [0.25 0. 0.] but [0.25 0.1875 0.1875] and the tree has fewer leaves than expected (about half of fits give 1 leaf instead of 2; np.bincount of n_leaves over 1000 fits prints roughly [0 ~500 ~500] instead of all 2-leaf trees).

The tree should always have two leaves and impurity [0.25 0. 0.] for the reproducer, i.e. the impurity decrease should be computed correctly and all trees should have two leaves (assert tree.tree_.n_leaves == 2 holds on every fit).
